message.content:
Build a JavaScript benchmark harness that compares three Parquet libraries running inside JS engines: **zig-parquet compiled to WebAssembly**, **hyparquet** (+ **hyparquet-writer**, pure JS), and **parquet-wasm** (Rust's arrow-rs compiled to WASM, used with **apache-arrow**). It must run in **Chrome**, **Firefox**, and **workerd** (Cloudflare's Workers runtime) and print one results table per runtime.

Work in `C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zig-parquet\.claude\worktrees\zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc` (Windows, Git Bash available; use forward slashes). Installed: node 24, npm 11, bun 1.3, system Chrome at `C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe`, system Firefox, and Playwright browser builds in `~/AppData/Local/ms-playwright` (chromium-1248, firefox-1538). Network access works for npm. Do NOT commit. Do NOT edit anything outside `bench/js/` (other agents are working in `bench/rust/`, `zig-parquet/`, `Makefile`, `.gitignore`). Tell me in your report what `.gitignore` lines and Makefile targets you need.

## Context: the native benchmark you are mirroring
Read `zig-parquet/bench/main.zig` first. Six scenarios, 1,000,000 rows by default, each phase run 3 times and the best time kept, checksum verified, fixed-width table output. Uncompressed files; numeric columns PLAIN, string columns dictionary-encoded (falling back to PLAIN when the dictionary gets large).

## Layout to create under `bench/js/`
```
package.json            private, "type": "module"; devDependencies pinned to exact latest versions:
                        hyparquet, hyparquet-writer, parquet-wasm, apache-arrow, playwright, workerd
package-lock.json       committed later
src/gen.js              data generation + expected checksum
src/checksum.js         (or inside gen.js) the checksum rule below
src/libs/zig.js         zig-parquet WASM adapter (contract below)
src/libs/hyparquet.js   hyparquet + hyparquet-writer adapter
src/libs/parquet-wasm.js parquet-wasm + apache-arrow adapter
src/bench.js            runtime-agnostic runner: runBench({ rows, libs, log, now }) -> results
src/entry-browser.js    browser entry
src/entry-worker.js     workerd entry (fetch handler)
index.html              loads the browser bundle
run-browsers.mjs        builds, serves, drives Chrome + Firefox via Playwright, prints tables
run-workerd.mjs         builds, starts workerd, fetches results, prints table
workerd.capnp           workerd config
README.md               short: how to run, what is measured, caveats
```
Build output goes to `bench/js/dist/` (gitignored). Use `bun build` for bundling (installed; `bun build src/entry-browser.js --outdir dist --target browser --format esm`, and similarly for the worker with wasm imports left external), unless it can't do something — then esbuild via npm is fine.

## Scenarios and data (src/gen.js) — generated once per scenario, untimed
PRNG = splitmix64 seed 42 (BigInt is fine, generation is untimed):
```
state = (state + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15n) & MASK64
z = state
z = ((z ^ (z >> 30n)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9n) & MASK64
z = ((z ^ (z >> 27n)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBn) & MASK64
return z ^ (z >> 31n)
```
f64 = `Number(next >> 11n) * 2**-53`; i32 = `BigInt.asIntN(32, next >> 32n)` as Number; i64 = `BigInt.asIntN(64, next)`; bool = `(next & 1n) === 1n`; idx = `Number(next % 1000n)`.
Scenario id / name / columns (canonical JS data, same order as the Zig bench):
- 0 `int64_plain`: `v` int64 required, BigInt64Array 0..n-1
- 1 `f64_plain`: `v` double required, Float64Array of f64 draws
- 2 `int64_nullable`: `v` int64 nullable: row i null when `i % 3 === 2`, else a counter starting at 0 that increments only on non-null rows. Canonical form: Array of (bigint | null).
- 3 `str_dict`: `s` string (nullable column, no nulls): `"dictval-" + String(i % 100).padStart(5, "0")`
- 4 `str_unique`: `s` string: `"row-" + i`
- 5 `mixed5`: `i32` Int32Array, `i64` BigInt64Array, `f64` Float64Array, `flag` Array<boolean>, `name` Array<string>; per row draw in order i32, i64, f64, bool, idx; name = `"category-" + String(idx).padStart(4, "0")`. All nullable columns, no nulls.

## Checksum (JS) — every reader must produce the same value
Float64 `Number` sum, in row order, over **column 0**: int64 → `Number(v)`, int32/double → `v`, string → UTF-8 byte length (all data is ASCII), null → 0. Compute `expected` from the canonical data. A read result is `{ rows, sum }`; it must equal `{ rows: n, sum: expected }` with `===`, otherwise that cell is an error (print `ERR`, keep going).

## What is timed (state this in README)
- **write** = canonical JS data → Parquet bytes as a `Uint8Array`. Includes any conversion the library needs (building Arrow tables, encoding strings to UTF-8, copying into WASM memory, copying the result out).
- **read** = `Uint8Array` file bytes → `{rows, sum}`. Every library must decode **all columns** (use each library's fastest natural API; columnar APIs are fine) and compute the column-0 checksum in JS from values that JS can see (typed arrays, Arrow vectors, or JS values).
- Best of 3 per phase, `performance.now()` unless the runtime freezes it (see workerd). Also record file size (MB, 1024²).
- Writer settings for all libraries: **no compression**, dictionary off for numeric/bool, on for strings, otherwise defaults. If a library can't express that, use its closest setting and say so in README and your report.

## Library adapters — each exports `{ name, init(assets), write(scenario, data) -> Uint8Array, read(bytes, scenario) -> {rows, sum} }` (async allowed)
### zig-parquet WASM (src/libs/zig.js)
A freestanding `zpbench.wasm` (no imports; exports its `memory`) is being written right now by someone else. Path: `zig-parquet/zig-out/bin/zpbench.wasm` (build: `make bench-wasm` from repo root — that target may not exist yet when you start; I will message you when it does. Build everything else first.) Exports contract (all pointers/lengths u32, i64 params are BigInt in JS):
```
zpb_alloc(len) -> ptr            // 8-byte aligned; 0 on OOM
zpb_free(ptr, len)
zpb_write(scenario, rows, a, b, c, d, e, f) -> i32   // output length, or negative on error
zpb_out_ptr() -> ptr             // output bytes from the last zpb_write
zpb_out_free()                   // free them
zpb_read(ptr, len) -> i32        // decode all rows/columns; returns row count or negative on error
zpb_col_ptr() -> ptr             // f64[rows]: column 0 per row as f64 (int → value, double → value, string → byte length, null → 0); valid until next zpb_read
zpb_col_free()
```
zpb_write inputs per scenario (each is a pointer into wasm memory that you allocated and filled; unused args = 0):
- 0 int64_plain: a = i64[rows]
- 1 f64_plain: a = f64[rows]
- 2 int64_nullable: a = i64[rows] (null slots: any value), b = u8[rows] validity (1 = present)
- 3, 4 strings: a = u32 offsets[rows + 1] (offsets[0] = 0), b = UTF-8 bytes
- 5 mixed5: a = i32[rows], b = i64[rows], c = f64[rows], d = u8[rows] bools (0/1), e = u32 offsets[rows + 1], f = UTF-8 bytes for `name`
Always re-create typed-array views after any call into wasm (memory can grow and detach old views). read: alloc + copy bytes in, zpb_read, sum a `Float64Array(memory.buffer, zpb_col_ptr(), rows)`, free. All of that is inside the timed read.

### hyparquet (src/libs/hyparquet.js)
Read with `hyparquet` (fastest columnar path that decodes all columns; check its README in node_modules for `parquetRead` with `onChunk`/columnar options, or `parquetReadObjects`; prefer columnar). Write with `hyparquet-writer` (`parquetWriteBuffer` or whatever its README documents) with codec UNCOMPRESSED and the dictionary rule above if supported. INT64 values are BigInt in hyparquet.

### parquet-wasm (src/libs/parquet-wasm.js)
Write: build an apache-arrow `Table` from canonical data (`tableFromArrays`/`makeVector`; strings as Utf8, nullable int64 with nulls), `tableToIPC(table, "stream")`, `parquetWasm.Table.fromIPCStream(ipc)`, `writeParquet(table, writerProperties)` with UNCOMPRESSED and the dictionary rule (look up `WriterPropertiesBuilder` in its .d.ts). Read: `readParquet(bytes)` → `.intoIPCStream()` → apache-arrow `tableFromIPC` → sum column 0 (for strings, use each Data chunk's `valueOffsets` to get byte lengths rather than materializing strings). Init with explicit wasm bytes / module (`initWasm` / default export with a `WebAssembly.Module` or bytes) — don't rely on `import.meta.url` fetching.

## Interop check (runs first, at 1000 rows, untimed)
For every scenario: each library writes; each library reads every other library's output; print a small matrix `writer → reader: ok/ERR`. This proves the files are real Parquet and the comparisons are fair. Mismatches are reported, not fatal.

## Runtimes
### Chrome + Firefox (run-browsers.mjs [rows])
- Build the browser bundle, start a tiny Node `http` server on a free port serving `bench/js/` (index.html, dist/, wasm assets) and the zig wasm (path from env `ZPBENCH_WASM`, default `../../zig-parquet/zig-out/bin/zpbench.wasm` relative to `bench/js`). Send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` (gives Firefox finer `performance.now()` precision) and `application/wasm` for .wasm.
- Playwright: Chrome = `chromium.launch({ channel: "chrome" })` (the installed real Chrome). Firefox = `firefox.launch()` (Playwright's Firefox build; if its version doesn't match the installed `playwright` package, run `npx playwright install firefox`). Headless is fine. Open `/?rows=N`, wait (timeout ≥ 15 min) for `window.__BENCH_DONE__`, then print the browser name + version (`browser.version()`) and the table the page produced. Run Chrome then Firefox sequentially, never in parallel.
### workerd (run-workerd.mjs [rows])
- Bundle `src/entry-worker.js` (ES module worker, `export default { async fetch(req) {...} }`), with the two wasm files as wasm modules (`import zigWasm from "./zpbench.wasm"` → `WebAssembly.Module`). `workerd.capnp` embeds the bundle and wasm modules; socket on 127.0.0.1:<port>; set a recent `compatibilityDate`. Start `node_modules/.bin/workerd serve workerd.capnp` (or `npx workerd serve ...`), GET `/?rows=N`, print the returned table, kill workerd.
- **Known trap:** Workers freeze `Date.now()`/`performance.now()` during pure CPU work (they only advance on I/O). Verify this first with a 200 ms busy loop. If frozen, try awaiting `new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` before each clock read and re-test. If that still doesn't advance, restructure so the runner times each phase from outside (one HTTP request per phase, generated data cached in module scope) and subtract an empty-request baseline. Report exactly what you found and which method you used.

## Output format (all runtimes)
Header line with runtime name + version, then per library a table with the native bench's column style:
```
lib            scenario        rows    write_ms  write_rows_per_s    read_ms  read_rows_per_s   file_MB
```
`n/a` for unsupported cells, `ERR` for failures. Also return the results as JSON (browser: `window.__BENCH_RESULT__`; worker: `?format=json`).

## Verify, in this order
1. Small runs first (`rows=10000`) for each runtime, all checksums ok, interop matrix all ok (or explain each ERR).
2. Then full runs at the default 1,000,000 rows: Chrome, then Firefox, then workerd, one at a time. If a library runs out of memory or takes > 5 min at 1M, note it and mark it n/a for that runtime rather than shrinking everything.

## Report
Package versions used; the three full tables (with runtime versions); the interop matrix; how you handled workerd timing; the `.gitignore` lines and Makefile recipes you need (targets `bench-js-browsers` and `bench-js-workerd`, run from the repo root, optional `ROWS`); every deviation from this spec and why.

# AGENTS.md

## Project Overview

zig-parquet is a native Parquet library written in Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 (one source tree). It provides read/write support for Parquet files, a C ABI, and a CLI tool (`pqi`). Read `README.md` for the full feature list and API examples.

## Project Structure

- `zig-parquet/` - Core Parquet library
- `cli/` - `pqi` CLI tool
- `zig-{zstd,brotli,lz4,gzip,snappy}/` - Pure Zig compression codec packages
- `test-files-arrow/` - Test files generated by Python (uses uv)
- `test-files-wild/` - Real-world Parquet files for compatibility testing

### Key Files

- `zig-parquet/src/lib.zig` - Library exports (package root)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/dynamic_reader.zig` - DynamicReader (schema-agnostic row reading)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/column_decoder.zig` - Column value decoding (encodings, levels, types)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/writer.zig` - High-level typed Parquet writer
- `zig-parquet/src/core/dynamic_writer.zig` - DynamicWriter (runtime-schema row writing)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/format.zig` - Parquet format types (re-exports from format/)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/safe.zig` - Safe casting/slicing helpers for untrusted data
- `zig-parquet/src/core/arrow_batch.zig` - Arrow C Data Interface bridge
- `zig-parquet/src/core/schema.zig` - Recursive schema for nested types + logical types
- `cli/src/main.zig` - pqi CLI entry point

### Documentation

- `ROADMAP.md` - Development phases and progress
- `zig-parquet/HARDENING.md` - Hardening guidelines
- `test-files-wild/README.md` - Test file validation status

### References

- Parquet format spec: https://github.com/apache/parquet-format
- Thrift Compact Protocol: https://github.com/apache/thrift/blob/master/doc/specs/thrift-compact-protocol.md

## Build & Test

**Always run from the repo root via `make`. Never `cd` into `zig-parquet/` or `cli/`** — the tool session preserves cwd across commands, so a stray `cd` strands later commands in the wrong directory. The Makefile's recipes handle the `cd` in a subshell so the outer cwd is unchanged.

`test`, `lib`, and `cli` accept `CODECS=<spec>` and `OPT=<ReleaseSmall|ReleaseFast|ReleaseSafe|Debug>` as make variables — don't add new fixed targets for each combination.

```bash
make help                              # List all targets with examples
make build                             # Build library + CLI (defaults)
make test                              # Library tests, all codecs (Zig preferred)
make test CODECS=zig-only              # Pure Zig codecs only (no C deps)
make test CODECS=c-only                # C/C++ codecs only
make test CODECS=none                  # Non-compression tests only
make test CODECS=c-zstd,zstd           # Cross-implementation (both zstd codecs)
make lib CODECS=c-brotli OPT=ReleaseSmall  # Size-measured release build
make example NAME=basic                # Build an example (NAME is required)
make example NAME=wasm_demo OPT=ReleaseSmall
make wasm                              # Verify WASM targets compile and link
make validate-wild                     # Validate pqi against wild files (failures)
make validate-wild-all                 # Validate pqi against wild files (all)
make bench ZIG=<path> ROWS=100000      # Benchmark harness (ReleaseFast, zig-only codecs); ROWS defaults to 1000000
make fmt ZIG=<0.16 zig>                # zig fmt across sources (0.16 only)
make clean                             # Remove .zig-cache and zig-out everywhere
```

`CODECS` values: `all` (default), `none`, `zig-only`, `c-only`, or comma-separated list from `zstd,snappy,gzip,lz4,brotli` (Zig) and `c-zstd,c-snappy,c-gzip,c-lz4,c-brotli` (C/C++).

## Dual-version rules

Every line under `zig-parquet/` and `cli/` must compile on both Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0.

| never write | write instead |
|---|---|
| `[_]T{v} ** n`, `.{v} ** n` | `@as([n]T, @splat(v))`, or `var a: [n]T = @splat(v);` |
| `"abc" ** n` | `comptime repeat.bytes("abc", n)` (`src/repeat.zig`) |
| `@cImport` / `@cInclude` | hand-written `const c = struct { extern fn ...; }` |
| `allocator.dupeZ(u8, x)` | `allocator.dupeSentinel(u8, x, 0)` |
| `std.hash.crc.Crc32`, `crc.@"CRC-32/ISO-HDLC"` | `std.hash.Crc32` |
| `b.args` / `run.addPassthruArgs()` in build.zig | `passArgs(b, run)` helper |
| `@backingInt`, `@fromBackingInt` | `@intFromEnum`, `@enumFromInt` |
| `allocator.print(...)`, `allocator.printSentinel(...)` | `std.fmt.allocPrint(...)`, `std.fmt.allocPrintSentinel(...)` |
| `std.heap.SafeAllocator`, `std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator` | `std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{})` |
| `std.meta.fields`, `std.meta.Int`, `std.meta.Tag` (new uses) | explicit types / `switch (T)` |

- **`zig fmt` only with 0.16** (`make fmt ZIG=<Z16>`). 0.17's fmt rewrites builtins to 0.17-only
  spellings. Do not let an editor format with 0.17.
- Do not follow the `zig-0-17` skill or main's 0.17-only code for spellings. Use the table above.
- Version gates (`builtin.zig_version`) are **not** allowed in `src/`. If you hit a 0.16/0.17
  difference not in the table, **stop and ask**.

Pick the toolchain per invocation with `ZIG=<path>` (default: `zig` on PATH), for example
`make test ZIG=C:/tools/zig-0.16.0/zig.exe` or `make test ZIG=C:/tools/zig-0.17.0/zig.exe`.
Non-0.16 toolchains use the gitignored `.zig17/cache` directory so their build caches stay separate.

## Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 — Key API Patterns

Always search the codebase for existing patterns before writing new code.

### std.Io Interface

Zig 0.17 uses a unified `std.Io` interface for all I/O. File operations require an `io: std.Io` parameter.

- **In `main`**: Accept `std.process.Init` — provides `init.io`, `init.gpa`
- **In tests**: Use `std.testing.io`
- **In library code**: Thread `io` through from caller

### File I/O

```zig
// Open/create files
const file = try std.Io.Dir.cwd().openFile(io, "path.parquet", .{});
defer file.close(io);

// Positional reads (replaces seekTo + read)
const n = try file.readPositionalAll(io, buffer, offset);

// Streaming writer
var buf: [8192]u8 = undefined;
var file_writer = file.writerStreaming(io, &buf);
const writer: *std.Io.Writer = &file_writer.interface;
try writer.writeAll(data);
try file_writer.interface.flush();
```

### ArrayList / ArrayListUnmanaged

```zig
var list: std.ArrayList(T) = .empty;     // NOT .init(allocator), NOT .{}
try list.append(allocator, item);         // allocator passed to ALL methods
const slice = try list.toOwnedSlice(allocator);
list.deinit(allocator);
```

### Memory-backed Writers

```zig
var out: std.Io.Writer.Allocating = .init(allocator);
defer out.deinit();
try out.writer.writeAll(data);
const owned = try out.toOwnedSlice();
```

### stdout / stderr

```zig
var buf: [256]u8 = undefined;
var stdout_writer = std.Io.File.stdout().writerStreaming(io, &buf);
const stdout = &stdout_writer.interface;
try stdout.writeAll("message\n");
try stdout_writer.interface.flush();
```

### Enum Conversion

```zig
// std.meta.intToEnum was removed — use std.enums.fromInt (returns ?T)
const codec = std.enums.fromInt(CompressionCodec, v) orelse return error.InvalidCodec;

// Use @intFromEnum / @enumFromInt (works on 0.16 and 0.17); never @backingInt / @fromBackingInt
const raw: u8 = @intFromEnum(status);
const restored: Status = @enumFromInt(raw);
```

### Target and formatting

```zig
const arch = @import("builtin").target.cpu.arch;

// std.fmt.allocPrint moved onto the allocator
const name = try std.fmt.allocPrint(allocator, "name_{d}", .{i});
```

### Custom Format Functions

```zig
pub fn format(self: @This(), writer: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
    try writer.print("{}", .{self.value});
}
```

### JSON Serialization

```zig
// Serialize
var out: std.Io.Writer.Allocating = .init(allocator);
errdefer out.deinit();
try std.json.Stringify.value(data, .{}, &out.writer);
return out.toOwnedSlice();

// Parse
var parsed = try std.json.parseFromSlice(MyData, allocator, json, .{});
defer parsed.deinit();
```

### ArenaAllocator

```zig
_ = arena.reset(.free_all);           // NOT arena.reset()
_ = arena.reset(.retain_capacity);
```

### Build Options (Conditional Compilation)

Compression codecs are controlled via `-Dcodecs=` (default: `all`).

Presets: `all` (C + Zig, Zig used by default), `c-only` (C/C++ only), `zig-only` (no C deps), `none`, or comma-separated list: `c-zstd,zstd,c-snappy,snappy,c-gzip,gzip,c-lz4,lz4,c-brotli,brotli`.

```zig
// Zig implementations (default); C implementations opt-in via c-only or c-<codec>
pub const zig_zstd = if (build_options.enable_zig_zstd) @import("zstd.zig") else {};
pub const zig_snappy = if (build_options.enable_zig_snappy) @import("snappy.zig") else {};
pub const zstd = if (build_options.enable_zstd) @import("c_zstd.zig") else {};
pub const snappy = if (build_options.enable_snappy) @import("c_snappy.zig") else {};
```

In tests, guard codec-specific tests with `supports_*` flags:

```zig
test "my zstd test" {
    if (!build_options.supports_zstd) return;
    // ...
}
```

### WASM Targets

- `export fn` does NOT use `callconv(.C)` on WASM — it won't compile.
- `wasm32-freestanding` won't work with `std.posix`, `std.Thread`, or `std.debug.print`. Use `wasm32-wasi`.

### Before Writing Code

1. Search the codebase for similar patterns first.
2. Compile incrementally — test after every 20-30 lines, not 200.
3. Read compiler errors carefully — Zig's errors are precise.
4. Never call deprecated methods — check for newer alternatives.

## Hardening Requirements

Both reader and writer handle **untrusted data**. Code must return errors instead of panicking on malformed input. See `zig-parquet/HARDENING.md` for full details.

### Never Use `@intCast` on External Data

Use `safe.zig` for all external data casting:

```zig
const safe = @import("safe.zig");

// BAD — panics if value doesn't fit
const size: usize = @intCast(header.page_size);

// GOOD — returns error if value is negative or out of range
const size = try safe.cast(header.page_size);
const count = try safe.castTo(u32, header.num_values);
```

### `catch unreachable` Requirements

When a value is mathematically guaranteed to fit, use `catch unreachable` but MUST include an inline comment explaining why:

```zig
const bit_idx: u3 = safe.castTo(u3, i % 8) catch unreachable; // i % 8 is strictly 0-7

if (value.len > std.math.maxInt(i32)) return error.ValueTooLarge;
const len = safe.castTo(i32, value.len) catch unreachable; // Checked against maxInt(i32) above
```

### Always Bounds-Check Before Slicing or Indexing

```zig
// BAD — panics if out of bounds
const value = data[offset..][0..length];

// GOOD
const value = try safe.slice(data, offset, length);
const item = try safe.get(T, data, index);
```

### Use Checked Arithmetic for External Values

```zig
// BAD — can underflow silently
const values_size = total_size - header_size;

// GOOD
if (total_size < header_size) return error.InvalidSize;
const values_size = total_size - header_size;

// GOOD
const total = std.math.add(usize, a, b) catch return error.Overflow;
```

### Return Context-Aware Errors

Use specific errors (`error.InvalidBitWidth`, `error.EndOfData`, `error.InvalidPageSize`) instead of generic `error.InvalidData`.

### Validate at API Boundaries

```zig
pub fn writeColumn(values: []const T) !void {
    if (values.len > std.math.maxInt(i32)) return error.TooManyValues;
    // ... proceed with encoding
}
```

### Common Safe Casting Helpers

- `safePageSize(i32) -> error{InvalidPageSize}!usize`
- `safeRowCount(i64) -> error{InvalidRowCount}!usize`
- `extractBitWidth([]const u8, usize) -> error{InvalidBitWidth, EndOfData}!u5`
- `safeTypeLength(?i32) -> error{InvalidTypeLength}!usize`
